anomalies.observed: PCA9685PW U2 pin 1 (A0) is on net +3.3V, while A1-A5 (pins 2, 3, 4, 5, 24) are on GND. With A0 high, the device address is 0x41, not 0x40.
anomalies.expected: The specification lists the PWM driver at I2C address 0x40, which requires all address pins A0-A5 to be low (GND).

evidence.quote: PWM/servo driver | FCCPeripherals | NXP PCA9685PW (I2C 16-ch PWM), I2C addr 0x40

anomalies.impact: The FCC firmware addressing the PCA9685 at 0x40 will get no ACK, so the servo/PWM outputs will not be driven.

anomalies.observed: The NAVC 25 MHz crystal HSE2 and its load/series network (C52, C53, R32) are on HSE_IN_NAVC / HSE_OUT_NAVC, which connect to no NAVC1 pin. NAVC1 PH0 and PH1 instead go to 2.2 uF capacitors C37 and C38 to GND.
anomalies.expected: The HSE crystal's two terminals should connect to the MCU's oscillator pins (PH0/PH1 on the F405).

evidence.quote: HSE crystal (both MCUs) | FCC / NAVC | ABM8G-25.000MHZ-4Y-T3 | `FCC.sch`, `NAVC.sch` notes "High Speed External Crystal"

anomalies.impact: The NAVC MCU has no working external clock, so it may fail to run at its intended frequency or at all.

parsed.summary: The strongest deviation is the PCA9685 A0 address strap tied to +3.3V, which moves the driver from the specified 0x40 to 0x41. The NAVC crystal nets also do not reach the MCU oscillator pins, though this may be inherited from the reference design.
